verdict.rationale: Grok documents a set of built-in connectors maintained by xAI for third-party services such as Salesforce, Gmail/Google Calendar, Google Drive and Microsoft Teams. Users connect each via OAuth, and can also add custom MCP connectors, so adding third-party connectors to the assistant is clearly supported. However, nothing shows a browsable directory or marketplace of third-party apps, and the built-in catalog appears to be xAI-curated rather than an open third-party ecosystem. Missing for 10: evidence of a browsable connector/app directory UI, third-party-published apps in a marketplace, independent hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a power-user, I can browse a directory of third-party apps and connectors and add them to the assistant

citations.quote: Built-in connectors are maintained by xAI and integrate natively with Grok. Each one authenticates via OAuth, so you connect once and Grok can access your data on demand.
When you add a custom MCP connector, Grok's servers need to reach your MCP server over the public internet.
Connect your tools so Grok can reach your email, files, and calendar right inside a chat.
The Google Drive connector lets Grok search, read, and manage files in your Google Drive.
